title: Develop with time against the queen
summary: Develop with an attack on the exposed queen, then occupy the centre and bring out your pieces.
goal: Develop with an attack on the exposed queen, then occupy the centre and bring out your pieces.

steps.text: Develop the b1 knight to c3 with an attack on the queen on d5.
After the queen moves, occupy the centre when sound instead of chasing it automatically.
Bring out the remaining pieces and prepare to castle, checking the queen's new threats.

jobs.text: The b1 knight can develop to c3 with an attack on the queen on d5.
The e-pawn has left the f1 bishop's diagonal open. Develop this bishop and prepare to castle when safe.
The d-pawn can occupy d4 after the queen retreats, giving your pieces central support.

opponent.text: The queen can retreat or give pressure from a5 or d6. A tempo gained against it is useful development, not a forced win of the queen.

notNow: Once the queen is no longer exposed, do not make weakening pawn moves just to attack it again.

mistakes.text: The bishop on d3 can be captured from d5. Do not sacrifice a developed piece without a concrete follow-up.

models.title: Develop with time against the queen

comments.text: Develop the knight with an attack on the queen on d5. Gain time for development rather than chasing the queen with repeated pawn moves.
Bring your pawn to d4. From d4 it controls e5. Keep watching Black's replies before advancing more pawns.
Bring your knight to f3. From f3 it controls d4 and e5. Keep watching Black's replies before advancing more pawns.
Bring your knight to e5. Keep your pieces working together and check the opponent's threats before the next move.
